newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds climb on US data, consolidation ahead.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds climb on US data, consolidation ahead.

text.p: Danish bond prices closed higher on Tuesday bolstered by good U.S. data but dealers saw a period of consolidation immediately ahead with prices staying at the new level.
"We will see consolidation tomorrow as the market adjusts to the new price levels," one dealer said.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 rose 0.39 point on the U.S. employment cost and durable goods data to finish 0.52 point up from the start at 109.70 and yield 6.52 percent in turnover of 2.1 billion crowns.
The benchmark's June future rose 0.30 point to 108.94 with 284 contracts traded. The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.80 point to 88.30.
The crown traded at 3.8070 per mark at 1430 gmt, virtually unchanged from the opening.
The 10-year yield gap with Germany was unchanged at 70 basis points.
The Central Bank was active on the market selling an unspecified amount of various state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
